messages:
Maria Gomez: Quick question — reviewing BYOK/HSM proxy for EU customers. Compliance asked for 7yr audit retention for key access events. Do we store any plaintext key material or just wrapped tokens in logs? Also what's the RBAC change surface to grant support access for on-call during incidents? :thinking_face:

Alex Chen: Short answer: no plaintext. We do NOT log key material. Logs contain key IDs, operation types, requestor principal, timestamp, and a boolean for wrapped_key_present. For BYOK the wrapped key blobs live in the customer's KMS or our encrypted store; runtime uses ephemeral session keys. For RBAC we want a clear separation: `key-admin` (create/rotate/wrap/unwrap), `key-ops` (operate, limited unwrap via JIT), `key-readonly` (audit-only).

Josh Patel: +1. Also note we had a near-miss where the proxy emitted full request bodies at TRACE level. Filing vuln triage to block TRACE in prod and to scrub any wrapped_key_blob fields.

Maria Gomez: Can someone paste the current log schema and the ILM/retention TTL we're applying for compliance customers?

SRE-Jen: Log schema (elasticsearch doc) below. Retention is handled via ILM; we can set 7y for specific customer indices. We also pseudonymize actor identifiers for GDPR unless customer opts into full auditable emails. Snippet:

```json
{
  "event": "hsm.operation",
  "key_id": "projects/1234/keys/abcd",
  "actor": "service-account:proxy@redwood",
  "actor_hash": "sha256:... (pseudonymized)",
  "operation": "generate_key|wrap|unwrap",
  "outcome": "success|failure",
  "request_id": "req-abc123",
  "region": "eu-west-1",
  "wrapped_key_present": true
}
```

And ILM policy example we attach to the customer's index pattern:

```json
PUT _ilm/policy/byo-hsm-7yr
{
  "policy": {
    "phases": {
      "hot": {"min_age":"0ms"},
      "warm": {"min_age":"30d"},
      "cold": {"min_age":"90d"},
      "delete": {"min_age":"2555d"}  
    }
  }
}
```

Alex Chen: Important operational constraints: `actor` entries must be RBAC-principled identities (no human creds in pods). For incident access we SHOULD NOT give engineers direct `key-admin`. Use JIT access via an approval flow — role `oncall-escrow` that injects short-lived unwrap tokens and logs the approval. Every JIT grant must emit a policy audit event.

Josh Patel: Vuln triage update — I created INC-2100 to track TRACE logging exposure and a PR to strip `wrapped_key_blob` from debug payloads. PR: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/pull/432 (internal). Also adding a unit-test to assert no sensitive fields in logs.

Compliance-Leah: For SOC2 we need: (1) retention policy evidence (ILM policy + cluster config), (2) separation of duties docs showing `key-admin` vs `oncall-escrow`, (3) chain-of-custody for cross-region key ops. For GDPR: pseudonymization rules + data subject request handling for actor hashes. Maria, please ensure the BYOK onboarding doc mentions default pseudonymization and opt-in paths.

audit-bot: AUTOMATED EVENT: policy_change user=Alex Chen action=ilm-policy-create target=byo-hsm-7yr ts=2087655000

Maria Gomez: Thanks — action items: Alex -> draft RBAC roles + JIT flow doc (RFC). SRE-Jen -> attach ILM policy to affected customer clusters and confirm pseudonymization pipeline (post confirmation in thread). Josh -> finish triage PR and link INC-2100. Compliance-Leah -> update BYOK onboarding checklist with retention + chain-of-custody notes. I'll also draft a short runbook paragraph for on-call.

SRE-Jen: Setting retention now for customer `acme-eu` index and scheduling a compliance drill. Will post confirmation when ILM is applied and snapshots are taken.

Alex Chen: KMS integration note: we NEVER hold unwrapped key material at rest. Wrapped blobs are stored (customer KMS or ours) and `Decrypt` happens only in isolated key-op pods that have no external network egress and strict RBAC. Those pods run short-lived processes and zero the memory after operation.

Josh Patel: IR note: during incident response we should snapshot metadata only (index names, request_ids, actor hashes). Add step to IR runbook to scrub ephemeral caches and confirm no HSM session keys remain on disk before handing artifacts to forensics.

Maria Gomez: :thumbsup: thanks everyone. Keeping thread open for the JIT RFC. I'll ping again in ~24h with a link to the draft doc: https://docs.redwood.com/byok/onboarding (draft).
